PLOS ONE article: questionnaires sent to 475 civil servants (405 returned) using a stated simple random sampling strategy, from federal/provincial/district public-sector organizations in Pakistan, respondents described as top-tier management. Workplace (reached through their employer/civil-service role) plus Representative (source's own random-sampling claim) plus Targeted/specific (senior officials). 3-item Political Support scale, 1-5 Likert, matches dictionary exactly.

construct_name: Oxford-Liverpool Inventory of Feelings and Experiences (O-LIFE)

German sample, N=498 (of 512 initially assessed); half recruited in lectures/via e-mail at a teacher-education program (Braunschweig University, 68% students) and half via mailing lists and Facebook. SWLS (Satisfaction With Life Scale) is genuinely named and described in this SPANE-validation paper as a convergent-validity measure -- 5 items, 7-point scale, German version -- so no dictionary/source contradiction despite SWLS being ancillary to the paper's main focus.

251 public primary/secondary school teachers from schools with a Digital Education Plan in Extremadura, Spain. Respondents are teachers reached through their employer/occupation -> Workplace (contrast with a study of their pupils, which would be Educational), plus Targeted/specific (schools restricted to those with the Digital Education Plan). 22 items, 6-point Never-Always frequency-of-practice scale -> Behavioral. No formally named instrument.
